what: Track A lane 3 on the claim "Z is Diophantine in Q" (Glazer et al., announced 2026-11-05): the claimant's four finite arithmetic suites (integer compiler, division polynomials over Q(√2), finite polynomial expressions, six-contact identities), re-derived clean-room from their prose and data with exact arithmetic of our own; their checker code not read.
undecided: The theorem (Z is Diophantine in Q) is undecided here: the main Lean target lean/Frozen/BoundedIntegerPolynomial.lean is unproved (its proof is `sorry`) and nothing in this record decides it. This record re-derives the claimant's four finite arithmetic suites; by their own README those suites do not establish the zero projection, the global height or restricted-converse inputs, or the natural precision polynomial's semantics.

rows.statement: Eq(A,B) ↦ A−B, And(F_i) ↦ Σ P_i², Or(F_i) ↦ Π P_i, empty And ↦ 0, empty Or ↦ 1: the polynomial vanishes exactly when the formula holds (over Q; leaves −1, 0, 1, 2, −1/2; And/Or of arity 0-2, two levels)
A | B ⟺ ∃d ∈ N: B = A·d, with 0 | B only for B = 0 (A, B ∈ [0,12])
A ≡ B (mod M) ⟺ ∃u,v ∈ N: A + M·u = B + M·v, M = 0 meaning equality (A, B, M ∈ [0,12]; witnesses in [0,12], enough here)
the power macro: for Q > 0 the unique P ∈ [0, m) with P + b·α_b(R) ≡ Q·α_b(R) + α_b(R+1) (mod m) is Q^R, and Q^R < m (Q, R ∈ [0,7]; Q = 0 is handled explicitly by the macro)

base = 2^(N+1), total = (1+base)^N, place = base^K, total = place·(base·u + C) + r with C < base, r < place: the unique C is binomial(N,K), 0 for K > N, and every binomial(N,j) < base (N ∈ [0,20], K ∈ [0,22])
A is a bitwise subset of B ⟺ binomial(B, A) is odd (A, B ∈ [0,63])
A and B have disjoint bits ⟺ binomial(A+B, A) is odd (A, B ∈ [0,63])
Z = X AND Y is the unique natural Z with X = Z+A, Y = Z+B and (Z,A), (Z,B), (A,B) pairwise disjoint, each disjointness by binomial parity (X, Y ∈ [0,63])
R ⊆ D and R < T ⟺ every base-B digit of R is < K and its digit q is 0 (c ∈ {1,2}, q ∈ {1,2,3}, every R < T)
S_i ⊆ F, Σ S_i = F and S_halt = T ⟺ exactly one state per slot and the halt state exactly at slot q (m ∈ {2,3} states, q ∈ {1,2}, every tuple of subsets of F)

completeness: for every accepting run (three machines of ours, inputs a ∈ [0,12]) with c chosen so that K exceeds every register value and B > m, every equation of §5 holds (BF+1 = F+BT, D+F = KF, the masks, K·N_j = (R_j+D) AND K·F, V_i = S_i AND N_j, S_i = V_i + W_i, the register and state equations)
K·N_j = (R_j + D) AND (K·F) gives exactly the packed nonzero indicator Σ_t [r_j(t) > 0]·B^t

soundness in a box: over every state sequence (halt only at slot q) and every register digit sequence (digits < K, digit q = 0), the solutions of all §5 equations are exactly the actual accepting run of length q, or none (machines clear, even, move; a ≤ 3; q ≤ 5; c ≤ 2)
